findings.title: IntoIter::drop double-frees remaining elements when an element's Drop panics
findings.evidence: Reachable from entirely safe code: `ThinVec::into_iter()` (line 2175) followed by dropping the returned `IntoIter<T>` enters `drop_non_singleton` (line 2544). At line 2547 `ptr::drop_in_place(&mut vec[this.start..])` is called BEFORE `vec.set_len_non_singleton(0)` at line 2548. If any element's destructor panics (a safe, user-supplied `impl Drop for T`), the slice drop-glue drops the remaining elements and then unwinds, so line 2548 never runs. The local `vec` (from `mem::replace` at line 2546) is still live and is dropped during unwinding via `Drop for ThinVec` (line 1917), which calls `ptr::drop_in_place(&mut this[..])` over the unchanged length: every element is dropped a second time, a classic double free (heap UAF/corruption for any T owning heap memory), and elements `[0..start]` already yielded to the caller via `next()` (line 2510) are dropped again while still owned by the caller. Demonstrated empirically: a 3-element ThinVec whose middle element's Drop panics produces 6 Drop invocations under catch_unwind (should be 3), and with Box payloads the process aborts on the double free. Upstream thin-vec 0.2.21 fixed this exact site by adding a DropGuard that runs `vec.set_len_non_singleton(0)` on unwind (test `test_panic_into_iter`), confirming the missing panic guard is the root cause.

findings.title: ThinVec::clear double-frees elements when an element's Drop panics
findings.evidence: `ThinVec::clear` (line 1082) calls `ptr::drop_in_place(&mut self[..])` at line 1084 and only zeroes the length afterwards at line 1085. If a `T::drop` panics (safe code, e.g. `v.clear()` on a vector of user types whose destructor can panic), the slice drop-glue destroys the remaining elements and unwinds, leaving `self.len()` unchanged while all elements are already destroyed. Unwinding then drops the still-live `ThinVec` through `Drop for ThinVec` (line 1917), which re-drops `[0..len]` — a double free of every element; if the panic is instead caught with catch_unwind, the same double free occurs at any later drop/use of the vector. Demonstrated empirically: clear() over 3 elements with one panicking Drop yields 6 Drop invocations instead of 3. Upstream thin-vec 0.2.21 fixed this site with a DropGuard that decrements len even on panic (test `test_panic_clear`), confirming the missing guard is the root cause.
